question: Does scalar DtN geometry require a Flat-Away metric selector, and does the actual original v210 state prescription select the charged source?
summary_de: Die skalare 2D-Randenergie ist innerhalb einer Konformalklasse exakt Weyl-invariant; eine physisch flache Innenmetrik muss für diesen Teil nicht ausgewählt werden. Der additive v290-Krümmungsoperator ist kein positiver masseloser skalarer DtN. Die ursprüngliche v210-Median-Kovarianz konvergiert auf fest identifizierten Fouriermoden auch beim tatsächlichen positiven Markenprofil stark gegen null. Ein geladener P1-Quellzustand samt Zeit und Erweiterungswahl wird nicht abgeleitet.
claim_scope: Massless scalar DtN applicability and fixed-mode limit of original state prescription only; original clock commutator checks remain valid
resolved: Scalar DtN boundary form depends on conformal class, not a choice of interior Weyl representative
Exact nullmode obstruction for the literal mean-zero additive curvature ansatz
Original v290 candidate has a negative eigenvalue and does not annihilate constants
Boundary metric weight remains relevant to DtN realization and spectral time
Actual positive v210 mark-profile median covariance tends strongly to zero under fixed Fourier embedding
kills: The original v290 cos4 additive operator is a positive massless scalar Laplace DtN
A unique flat interior metric must be chosen before determining scalar 2D Dirichlet energy within a fixed conformal class
The v210 median prescription reconstructs a nonzero chiral Hardy covariance in its fixed Fourier-mode limit
A scalar spectral function of |D| alone selects positive rather than negative directed modes
not_derived: Original P1 selection of the marked conformal domain and boundary density
Graded local source field algebra and spin structure
P1 charged vacuum covariance and same-space physical time generator
Selection of E8 local extension from neutral D8 data alone
assumptions: Conformal theorem uses the potential-free scalar 2D Laplacian, not a massive or spinorial operator
Conical deformation claim preserves the chosen domain by support away from singularities
Covariance limit uses fixed Fourier identification and the actual original median prescription
Moving Fermi-point identifications or new scaling limits are not excluded or silently introduced
